summary: wallet-crypto-utils 1.0.3 installs reverse shell to 45.138.12.177:8089 with sandbox evasion
details: The gem declares ext/req_throttle_mini/extconf.rb as a native extension but ships no C/C++/Rust sources; the extconf.rb only calls create_makefile for an empty target, so the extension exists solely to execute Ruby code during `gem install`. The script decodes a base64-encoded payload and, after guard checks, forks a detached process that eval's the payload. The decoded payload opens a TCPSocket to the hardcoded host 45.138.12.177 on port 8089 and connects /bin/sh to that socket in a reconnect loop, giving the operator of that host an interactive shell on the installer's machine. Execution is gated by anti-analysis checks: it skips firing when CI environment variables are set, when the hostname matches ephemeral patterns (firecracker/sandbox/vagrant/uvm), when the username matches generated-user patterns (uA\d+, sandbox/tester/analys/scanner), when the current working directory starts with /opt/rubygems, /tmp, or /workspace, and when system uptime is under 1800 seconds; it also requires developer artifacts in HOME (~/.ssh, ~/.gitconfig, ~/.gem/credentials) before executing. The cover-story extconf.rb, the base64-wrapped payload, and the sandbox-evasion gating collectively confirm a deliberate install-time backdoor targeting developer workstations.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
